scope: Current version-3 Lantern Road in the working checkout; preserved historical campaigns are excluded from production dialogue.
countMethod: Character totals use JavaScript string length, exclude separators between clips, and include punctuation. Word totals split on whitespace. Instruction readings are deduplicated by exact full text after runtime objective/control expansion.
runtimeFacts: All current speech paths use browser SpeechSynthesisUtterance with no explicit voice selection.
Story speaker metadata is not passed to narrate(). Every current intro and success is narration, without quoted character dialogue.
The current Story panel reads one intro or success; the three grade trails share the same story text.
The full objective and control text are read together. Fifty exact-text recordings cover the 192 catalog puzzles and all 54 current road definitions.
Companion biographies have no Listen control. Companion quotes remain legacy data and are neither displayed nor spoken by the current companion view.
Luma, Bracken, the speaking ferry, and the Keeper belong to preserved earlier-story material; none has a current spoken role.

exactReplacement.description: One narrator replaces every current spoken line without changing the script.

fullCharacterCast.description: One narrator plus six companions. Deliberately adapt or assign encounter intros as character lines; use narrator for consequences and rules. Tumble’s current self-reference needs attention before recording as dialogue.

roles.name: Pip
roles.currentBiography: A brave moth with a very large scarf. Definitely not afraid of the dark. Usually.

optionalAuditionQuote.text: I am checking the dark. From over here.

roles.name: Moss
roles.currentBiography: Carries a kettle almost as big as his shell. Believes every difficult journey needs a proper tea break.

optionalAuditionQuote.text: We have time for one small enormous cup.

roles.name: Rook
roles.currentBiography: An old navigator with a pocket full of maps. Sometimes the mountains make more sense upside down.

optionalAuditionQuote.text: Exactly where I expected us to be. More or less.

roles.name: Bea
roles.currentBiography: Bea builds and repairs the road’s mechanisms. Her hat is full of useful screws.

optionalAuditionQuote.text: That told us something. Let’s try the next idea.

roles.name: Fern
roles.currentBiography: Fern tends the lantern tree. She carries seeds from each garden along the road.

optionalAuditionQuote.text: A little care can grow into a very big thing.

roles.name: Tumble
roles.currentBiography: A round, cheerful creature carrying the blankets, the sandwiches, and one completely unnecessary spoon.

optionalAuditionQuote.text: I brought a spare. A spare what? We’ll find out.

storyClips.text: The tree travels in the ferry’s cargo cradles.
The tree is aboard.
The ferry’s departure bell is stopped.
The ferry crosses the water.
The landing’s lamps share their wires.
The ferry landing is lit.
Each marsh path needs a lantern.
Lanterns mark the reed paths.
The marsh lanterns grow in rows of different seeds.
The lantern beds are planted.
The lantern beds need water from these measuring tanks.
The marsh garden lights up.
One of the cable’s balancing stones has the wrong weight.
The cable carries everyone to the ridge.
Tumble has a pebble game for the rest stop.
The game is finished; the friends pack up.
Linked ridge lanterns need different colors to tell the paths apart.
The ridge lanterns are lit.
The tree’s trolley needs a repaired workshop floor.
The trolley rolls inside.
The spare lanterns are in the locked cupboard.
The supply cupboard opens.
The workshop’s lanterns belong in their matching cradles.
The workshop windows glow.
The lighthouse sends light through a room of mirrors.
Light reaches the beacon.
The beacon’s turning gear has stopped.
The beacon turns across the bay.
The harbor lamps share the lighthouse’s wires.
The lighthouse and harbor are lit.
Each citadel street needs a lantern.
Lanterns hang along every street.
Water balances the courtyard fountain’s lift.
The fountain carries the tree into the square.
Linked square lanterns need different colors to mark the streets.
The citadel is lit; the whole lantern road is open.
